slides.headline:
Eight seats.
Two MICHELIN stars.
slides.subline: Sosuheon, Manri-dong — a sushi counter inside an old Seoul hanok, promoted to Two Stars in the MICHELIN Guide Seoul & Busan 2026

slides.label: seats at the counter — and one of only ten Two-Star restaurants in Seoul
slides.note: The MICHELIN Guide Seoul & Busan 2026 promoted Sosuheon from one star to two. Korean coverage of the ceremony puts the city's Two-Star count at ten, with Mingles again the only Three-Star restaurant in Korea. Chef Park Kyung-jae serves two seatings a day at an eight-seat counter, so roughly sixteen people eat here on a full day. Korean press describes him as the first, and so far only, chef in Korea holding two stars for sushi. Sources: guide.michelin.com, Stripes Korea, Seoul Finance, Longblack

items.t: A hanok, not a basement counter
items.d: The MICHELIN Guide's own entry places Sosuheon inside a traditional hanok set against Seoul's modern skyline, and calls it a quiet counterpoint to the city around it
Guests watch the nigiri being formed from a counter of eight. Korean press reports two seatings a day, one at lunch and one at dinner
The guide describes refined seasonal courses ahead of the sushi — cod roe with hairy crab, grilled hairtail — with a final bowl of matcha closing the meal
The name is written in hanja built on the character for a bare hand. Korean profiles of the chef translate it as roughly "the house of clean hands" — a claim about method rather than about the food

slides.title:
He already had two stars.
They were someone else's.
slides.body:
Park Kyung-jae did not arrive at two stars in 2026. He arrived there twice.

Korean profiles trace his start to February 1989, at a small Japanese restaurant in Banpo, then twelve years at Ariake, the Japanese room inside Seoul's Shilla Hotel. He went on to be head chef at Kojima in Cheongdam-dong, and held two MICHELIN stars there. In 2023 the guide gave him its Seoul Mentor Chef Award — a prize for teaching, not for cooking.

All of it was earned under someone else's sign. In 2024 he opened Sosuheon in a roughly ninety-year-old hanok in Manri-dong, near Seoul Station, with his own name on it and eight seats in the room. The 2026 guide moved it from one star to two.

The non-obvious part is the room size. Reaching that tier usually means scaling up. He went the other way: fewer covers, one pair of hands, a house named for keeping them clean.

items.d: Manri-dong 2-ga, in the hills just west of Seoul Station. Phone 0502-1933-1337, per its DiningCode listing
DiningCode lists 12:00–21:00 with a break from 14:30 to 18:30; press coverage describes Saturday as lunch only. Reservation-only, and the guide's site does not take bookings — confirm directly
The listed omakase prices, with corkage at 200,000 won a bottle. This is one of the more expensive rooms in the city, and worth knowing before you book
A promotion to two stars tends to move reservations quickly, and there are only sixteen covers on a full day. Availability, not price, is usually the binding constraint

slides.text:
This is research, not a personal review.
Every fact here comes from published sources, checked in September 2026.
slides.by:
We have not eaten here. Whether an omakase at this price is worth it to you is your call, not ours.
Prices, hours and menus change without notice, and a freshly promoted counter can be booked out for months — confirm before you go.

caption:
A chef who already held two MICHELIN stars left, opened a room with eight seats, and earned two more.

Sosuheon sits in an old hanok in Manri-dong, near Seoul Station. The 2026 guide promoted it from one star to two — one of only ten Two-Star rooms in the city.

We haven't eaten here, and 300,000 won lunches are yours to judge.

Sources in the last slide.
